unresolvedQuestions: 1. ANSWERED AND MEASURED — the critic's own instruction was 'measure why the `wide` pose does not get the warm/cool split before touching any light'. It does get it, at PIXEL scale, and it does not get it at BOX scale, and the reason is that nothing casts a shadow there. Evidence, model-free: binning every pixel of a plateau region by luminance and reading mean hue per bin, `wide` at 25 m runs R/B 0.610 (darkest octile) -> 1.623 (brightest), and the acceptance box at 33 m runs 0.749 -> 1.302 — a warm-bright / cool-dark correlation, i.e. a real directional warm key modulating micro-relief. The comparison instrument is `sun`'s near plaza over the same binning: 0.556 -> 2.107. So the key is arriving on the plateau; what is missing is any metre-scale occluder to organise it. The five acceptance boxes are 60x40 px = 2.0 x 1.3 m of ground each and they average that pixel-scale split away.

2. DISPROVED — round 17's peter-panning arithmetic, which is what the round-18 exemption was granted on. Round 17 wrote that cascade 1's `normalBias` of 18.1 cm 'at a 13 deg sun detaches a shadow by 78 cm' via h/tan(13 deg). That double-counts. three offsets the RECEIVER by b*N in shadowmap_vertex; the ground point that lands on the same shadow-map texel is Q = P + bN + tL with t = -b/(N.L) = -4.44b, i.e. Q is 0.784 m DOWNSUN of P. So the map's content is painted 0.784 m UPSUN — the shadow overruns the caster's own base rather than detaching from it, and the tip is 0.78 m short. The depth margin the offset buys is 4.22b = 0.765 m, plus |shadow.bias| * depthRange = 1.6 texel = 0.181 m, total 0.946 m; against a vertical pole the receiver-to-blocker depth difference is d/cos(13 deg) = 1.0263 d, so the shadow is erased only for d(Q) < 0.922 m, i.e. d(P) < 0.138 m. Net contact erosion is 14 cm, not 78 cm. Normal-offset bias is doing exactly the job it exists for. DO NOT spend a round reducing it.

3. DISPROVED — cascade-1 texel density is not the mechanism either, so I declined to spend the memory the exemption offered. Executed values, printed by the new report from the real class at the real `wide` framing: cascade 0 [0.12, 14.24] m, radius 17.89 m, texel 2.33 cm, normalBias 3.73 cm, PCF 5.13 cm; cascade 1 [14.24, 70.00] m, radius 86.99 m, texel 11.33 cm, normalBias 18.12 cm, PCF 15.86 cm; fade band (56.0, 67.9) m. Now price the largest caster that fails: the outer torii at z = 68 is 3.35 m tall with a 2.9 m kasagi, sits at 21 m view depth (squarely cascade 1, kagCascadeWeight = 1, kagFade = 1), and its kasagi shadow must paint a 2.9 m x 0.35 m bar — 26 x 3 shadow texels, 120 x 15 screen px — centred at screen (580, 898). A 26-texel-long feature is not lost to an 11.3 cm texel, and a 0.35 m shaft is not lost to a 15.9 cm PCF radius (0.317 m across, narrower than the shaft). Raising resolution cannot turn nothing into something. THE FAILURE IS BINARY, NOT A QUALITY SHORTFALL.

4. THE MEASURED NULL RESULT that items 2 and 3 rest on. Two stone lanterns (height 2.05 m, Level.js:797) at 21.1 m and 21.5 m, i.e. cascade 1 and well inside the fade band, each of which must throw an 8.9 m shadow 84% screen-left and 54% into the screen. Sampled along the exact downsun ground axis at t = 0.6 / 1.2 / 2.5 / 5.0 m from each base with 42x16 boxes: p50 104.1 / 83.9 / 56.5 / 43.5 (left lantern) and 88.5 / 68.0 / 55.7 / 56.9 (right). Monotone falloff of the additive spill decal, no dip at any point. Open plateau at that depth is 35.8 and a fully shadowed value would be about 35.8 / 1.846 = 19.4. Cross-checked by eye at 1:1 on a p2-p98 contrast-stretched crop of the same region (`0.30,0.80,0.30,0.19`), where the only feature at each base is a bright halo and the ground downsun is ordinary mottle. The same crop of shots/phone-wide-r16.png is identical, so this is a standing property, not a round-17 regression.

5. WHERE IT IS NOT — cascade 0 demonstrably works. In `sun` the great torii's near pillar (camera at z 36.9, gate at z 38.5, so 2-3 m out, cascade 0) throws a hard diagonal across the near flagstone, and the critic's own two boxes read it: lit (760,970 180x100) meanRGB [91.2,62.2,49.2] scene-linear R/B 2.435 against shadowed (1010,1055) [50.0,50.1,55.7] R/B 0.868, luminance ratio 1.447. So shadows are produced under 14.2 m and are absent over it. `wide` contains essentially no cascade-0 ground at all — view depth 14.2 m is below the bottom edge of that framing — which is why this framing shows the failure cleanly and the other four hide it.

6. ROUTING FOR THE BINARY FAILURE. Not localisable further without a runtime probe, which this round was forbidden to launch. The new `cascadeReport.mapReady` + `_warnOnce` settles half of it for free on the next verification capture: if cascade 1 warns, three never allocated its map and the fault is in this file's light/frustum setup (mine); if it does not warn, the map exists and the fault is the caster set, i.e. `Level.js:_realizeShadowProxies` (which turns castShadow OFF on every opaque static cell and substitutes one merged 192 m proxy per cell — Level.js:1389-1445) or `Props.js:InstancedProto.realize` (which lets only the single heaviest-by-index part of a prototype cast — Props.js:1142). The decisive A/B, if the coordinator wants it in one capture: force `shadowCascades: 1` at MEDIUM in src/core/Quality.js and re-shoot `wide`. The whole frame then falls in cascade 0. If the torii bar appears at screen (580,898), the fault is cascade-1-specific and mine; if it does not, the fault is the caster set and it is not mine.

7. FALSIFICATION OF MY OWN ROUND-17 HEADLINE PREDICTION, reported as required. Round 17 predicted the `wide` ground R-B-versus-fog ladder slope would flatten from -2.94 to 'roughly -0.6' and called it 'the single most diagnostic number for this change'. Re-run on the identical eight boxes, identical column (x-frac 0.815, y-frac 0.955 down to 0.640), r16v1 against r17v2: -2.929 (r = -0.92) -> -1.886 (r = -0.84), n = 8. The fix delivered 36% of the predicted 80% move. Direction right, magnitude wrong by a factor of three. The residual is the airlight's AMOUNT, not its colour: at f = 8-13% the term still paints a 12-code R-B ramp across 29 m of dead-flat, uniformly-lit plateau.

8. WHY I DID NOT FINISH THAT ANYWAY. Cutting the near-field airlight amount is the obvious next Sky.js move and it is the wrong move for THIS finding: fitting the ladder gives R-B = 19.98 - 1.886 f, so scaling f down on short ground rays warms every one of the five acceptance boxes (e.g. a 45% cut takes the ladder ends from +7.0 and -4.9 to +14.7 and +5.9). Criterion (2) explicitly asks for two of the five to go the other way, to B >= R. It would satisfy the critic's third symptom and breach the criterion that replaced the one round 17 was accused of gaming. Held, with the transfer function recorded so a later round can spend it deliberately.
acceptanceCriteria: CRITERION (1) — 'the five non-lantern boxes must span >= 25 code values of p50 (currently 10.1)'. NOT MET, and PROVEN UNREACHABLE FROM THESE TWO FILES IN THIS POSE. Measured on r17v2: 38.1 / 42.2 / 45.0 / 47.6 / 48.2, span 10.1, unchanged. The proof: all five sit at a constant view depth of 33.3 m on ground that WORLD.PLATEAU_RADIUS 78 holds dead flat at 812 m, so a 25-code span needs some of them in cast shadow and some in sun — the coordinator's own framing, and the 1.8459x ceiling re-measured above does reach 26.7 codes. For a box to be shadowed by an object of height h, that object must stand at box + (3.825h, 2.032h) in world XZ (sun (0.86, 0.225, 0.457), elevation 13 deg). Enumerated: box 3 (16.1, 54.3) needs a 1.15 m object at (21, 57) — screen (1934, 875), cropped and confirmed bare ground; at 10 m upsun it needs (25, 59) which is screen (2180, 911), still bare; past that the required ground leaves the frame entirely — 20 m upsun of boxes 3/4/5 projects to screen x 2846 / 3588 / 3857 against a 2532 px frame. Boxes 1 and 2 run off the BOTTOM edge instead: 20-30 m upsun projects to screen y 1009-1171 against a 1170 px frame. Checked against LAYOUT (src/world/Level.js:45-62): the three torii are all at x = 0 (z 68.0 / 54.0 / 38.5) and every building is at |x| <= 21 and z <= 30, i.e. downsun of the row, not upsun of it. There is nothing to cast, and the ground that would carry a caster is mostly not in the frame. OWNER: src/core/Cinematic.js (the pose) or src/world/Level.js (dressing upsun of the acceptance row). See open item 8 in HANDOFF.md — `wide` is front-lit by construction, 122.8 deg off the view axis.

CRITERION (2) — 'at least one of the five must have R exceeding B by >= 15 codes AND at least two must have B >= R'. NOT MET, and ARITHMETICALLY UNSATISFIABLE from any aerial-perspective change, which is the only axis Sky.js has at constant depth. Measured R-B on r17v2: -0.8 / +3.9 / +6.8 / +2.8 / +1.5. The five boxes span f = 8.9 to 11.7% of fog. Fitting the frame's own transfer on the eight-box ladder gives R-B = a - b*f with a = 19.98 and b = 1.886 code per 1% of f (n = 8, r = -0.84). Satisfying 'box 3 (f 8.9) >= +15' and 'boxes 1 and 5 (f 11.4, 11.7) <= 0' simultaneously requires a - 8.9b >= 15 and a - 11.4b <= 0, hence b >= 6.0 and a >= 68.4 — a chroma gradient 3.2x the measured one AND ground reading R-B +68 at zero fog. A b of 6.0 means an airlight far bluer than the one round 16's chroma restoration produced, which is the blue-shift blocker round 17 was dispatched to fix. The criterion is asking for a lit/shadow split and can only be paid for with one. Same routing as (1).

CRITERION (3) — 'the base ring must no longer be a local maximum, and some 42x16 box within 40 px of a lantern base on the downsun side must read p50 below 35.8'. NOT MET, and it is TWO findings with two different owners. (a) The base ring is not a Lighting term at all: it is `lantern-pool`, `Level.js:805`, a `groundLightPool` decal placed one-per-lantern with `castShadow:false, receiveShadow:false`, confirmed by r17v2 telemetry `lanternSpill { count 24, matchesLanternCount true, blending 2 (additive), opacity 0.38, depthWrite false }`. An additive decal is a local maximum by construction and NO shadow term can stop it being one, because the shadow multiplies `directLight.color` and the decal is added after it. That half routes to src/world/Level.js. (b) The second half does need a lantern shadow, and item 4 above measures that there is none to darken: 40 px at that depth is 0.79 m, and the downsun axis reads p50 104.1 at 0.6 m and 83.9 at 1.2 m against the 35.8 the criterion sets. Blocked on the binary cascade-1 failure in item 6.

risks: The `_warnOnce` fires on `light.shadow.map` being null, which three populates lazily on the first shadow render. Thirty frames is comfortably past that in any real boot but it is a heuristic, not a proof: a build that stalls its first shadow render past 30 frames would emit a false positive once. It is warn-once and touches nothing, so the worst case is one misleading log line.

`cascadeReport` is a new public surface on LightingSystem. Nothing reads it yet, so it is dead weight until a probe or capture.mjs picks it up. It is 8 numbers per cascade written on an already-hot path and pre-allocated, so the cost is real but negligible; if round 19 decides nobody will ever read it, delete it rather than leave it unread.

This round shipped no pixel change. That is deliberate — every candidate was eliminated by measurement, and the project's own rule is that acting on an unverified mechanism is how round 5 shipped a fix round 6 measured as a no-op — but it does mean the `wide` blocker is going into round 19 exactly as the round-18 critic left it, and the coordinator should route it to Cinematic.js/Level.js rather than back here.

Item 7's falsification is on a slope measured across a single column that changes ground material partway up (detail falls from ~9 to ~2.6 above y-frac 0.653, which is the 34 m grass-instancing radius). The r16v1-to-r17v2 comparison is on the IDENTICAL boxes so the material change cancels, but the absolute slope value carries that mixture and should not be quoted as a pure air measurement.
rollback: One revert of a single commit touching only src/render/Lighting.js. The change is additive diagnostics: delete `this.cascadeReport` and `this._shadowProbeFrames` from `_build`, the `rep` block at the end of `frameShadows`, and the probe block in `update`. No rendering value is involved, so the frame is byte-identical either way.
